transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

My mind just won’t stop going over everything that could go wrong at work, and I can’t seem to turn the worrying off anymore. It has gotten to the point where I feel constantly overwhelmed, so a colleague suggested I come speak with someone.
Did this worrying start after a specific stressful event or change in your life, or has it been more of a general pattern across many situations? About how long has it been going on?

It really started building up a little over a year ago after I was promoted to lead a major digital preservation initiative at the library. While it began with work pressures, it has now spread to other areas of my life, like constantly worrying about my nieces' college funds even when I'm off work.

If the work promotion and project pressure were removed, do you think the worrying would mostly go away, or would you still find yourself worrying excessively about many different parts of life? Has the anxiety felt tied mainly to that stressor, or more free-floating across situations?

I honestly think the worrying would still find a way to latch onto other things now. Even when I'm away from work trying to relax in my garden, my mind drifts to fretting about my finances or whether I've ruined my nieces' college options. It feels much more free-floating and hard to escape now, rather than just being about my job.
Over the past 6 months or more, have you been feeling worried like this on most days? And when the worry starts, is it hard to control or stop it?

Yes, it has been happening almost every single day for over a year now. Once the "what ifs" start, it is incredibly difficult to shut them off, and I'll find myself pacing or obsessively rechecking work drafts even though I know it's irrational. I just can't seem to pull my mind away from it.

Along with the constant worry, have you often had symptoms like feeling restless or on edge, getting tired easily, trouble concentrating, irritability, muscle tension, or problems sleeping? If so, which ones have been happening most days?

Yes, I've been struggling with several of those almost every day. My shoulders and neck constantly feel like concrete, and I lie awake until 1 or 2 a.m. only to wake up at 4 with my jaw clenched. I also can't seem to concentrate anymore; my mind drifts when I try to read or catalog, and I've even gone completely blank mid-sentence during meetings.
How much is this anxiety interfering with your daily life, like your work performance, relationships, or taking care of things at home? Can you give one or two examples?

It's interfering a great deal; at work, I've started missing internal deadlines and even avoiding leading community events because I'm too anxious or busy rechecking things. In my personal life, I've stopped going to yoga and hikes, and I keep turning down invitations from friends and family because I feel I have to stay home and obsessively review my work.

This pattern is most consistent with generalized anxiety disorder.
